headline: 07 IST / Korea Times / TRT World) -- Ansar Allah attack Aden, seat of the Saudi-backed Yemeni government, after accusing Saudi
dek: After the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two Ansar Allah missiles aimed at Taif and Yanbu on Saturday, explosions were heard in Aden. The Ansar Allah claimed they targeted 'Saudi enemy concentrations at the so-called Al-Nasr camp and the naval base in Aden' (Saree).
sources: Ansar Allah military spokesman Yahya Saree; Ansar Allah-run Al-Masirah; Yemeni government interior ministry via Saba; Yemeni information ministry (X post); Saudi-led coalition statement; AFP
fault_line: Is the Aden strike a widening of the war to the government's own seat -- proving no Yemeni city is safe -- or a symbolic retaliation whose disputed targets show both sides inflating the hit?

sections.what_happened: After the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two Ansar Allah missiles aimed at Taif and Yanbu on Saturday, explosions were heard in Aden. The Ansar Allah claimed they targeted 'Saudi enemy concentrations at the so-called Al-Nasr camp and the naval base in Aden' (Saree). The Yemeni government gave a different target account: its interior ministry said two ballistic missiles hit the coast guard headquarters at the ministry compound and a third hit a coast guard building in al-Tawahi; the information ministry reported renewed ballistic attacks on Aden airport and a port in al-Tawahi, with no casualty/damage details. The Ansar Allah accused Saudi strikes of killing 16: at least 4 in a Sanaa house, 6 women + 1 child at a cement-factory workers' residence in Sanaa governorate, and a family of 5 in Hodeida (Al-Masirah). Separately, the US missions in the UAE and Riyadh said US travel advisories for both Gulf countries were updated Saturday to reflect increased potential Ansar Allah armed attacks (Korea Times).
sections.what_verified: AFP wire story carried by The Hindu, Korea Times, LBC and Aaj TV counts as ONE family (AFP); TRT World reporting of the Yemeni government account is a second distinct family. Ansar Allah/Al-Masirah and Yemeni government statements are the primary sources for their own claims, not independent confirmation of each other.
sections.what_disputed: Target dispute is the story's fault line: Ansar Allah claim a Saudi naval base + Al-Nasr camp; the Yemeni government says coast guard HQ, a second coast guard building, the airport and a port -- and makes no mention of the base near the airport. No casualty or damage figures for the Aden attack itself have been published by either side; the 16-killed figure covers Sanaa/Hodeida strikes only and rests on Al-Masirah. An undated Aden-airport missile CCTV clip circulating socially was already flagged as stale in totw-20261024-1500-06 -- it is NOT evidence for this attack.
sections.why_matters: Lead with the target dispute, not one side's version: Saree's naval-base claim on screen against the interior ministry's coast-guard/airport account, then the 16-killed Sanaa/Hodeida accusation clearly labelled as Ansar Allah-attributed. The widening frame: this is the first Ansar Allah strike on the government's interim capital in this round, hours after the Taif/Yanbu interceptions already recorded at 1500.
